e.etymology: A Latin American phonetic spelling of the English pronunciation of Jacob, from Hebrew Ya'aqov, traditionally holder of the heel or supplanter.
The Spanish form of Athena, the Greek goddess of wisdom, craft and war and the patron of Athens. The origin of the goddess's name is unknown.
A spelling of Benny or Bennie, pet forms of Benjamin, Benedict and Bennett. For girls it also shortens names like Benita and Bernadette.
A short form of names ending in -riella, such as Ariella, Gabriella and Mariella, used on its own.
In Estonia Kaido is a masculine form of Kaidi, a variant of Katariina. Its recent American use follows Japanese kaido, a main road or sea route, and Kaido, a pirate emperor in the anime One Piece.
namesakes: Kaido (fearsome pirate emperor in the anime One Piece)

e.etymology: The English word for a hill of windblown sand, borrowed from French and Dutch. Its use as a name rose with the 2021 and 2024 films of Frank Herbert's science fiction novel Dune.

assoc.t: Frank Herbert's sci-fi novel and its blockbuster films

e.etymology: A respelling of the English word chrome, the shiny chromium plating on cars and motorcycles, from Greek chroma, color.
e.note: Sounds identical to chrome, the metal finish, and Chrome, the Google web browser.

e.etymology: Coined in the late 1800s, probably as a variant of Wilma or Vilma, short forms of Wilhelmina, shaped by the sound of Thelma and Selma.
namesakes: Velma Dinkley (the brainy sleuth in Scooby-Doo)
Velma Kelly (vaudeville murderess in the musical Chicago)

e.etymology: A pet form of names ending in -nette or -etta, such as Annette, Jeannette, Antoinette and Henrietta. It was a top-100 name for American girls in the late 1800s.
namesakes: Nettie (Celie's sister in The Color Purple)

e.etymology: A spelling of Eileen, the English form of Irish Eibhlín, which came from the Norman French name Aveline. It has also long been treated as an Irish form of Helen.
An English variant of Chantal, taken from the title of Saint Jeanne de Chantal. The place name comes from Old Occitan cantal, stone, though the name is often linked to French chant, song.
The name of Toyota's luxury car brand, launched in 1989 and itself an invented word. Parents took it up for girls in the 1990s alongside Alexis and Lexi.

e.meaning: of the Gauts, a Germanic people
e.etymology: A spelling of Jocelyn shaped by Joyce. Jocelyn comes from the Norman name Joscelin, from a Germanic name referring to the Gauts, a Germanic people.
A double-n spelling of Tatiana, the feminine of the Roman family name Tatianus, from Tatius, of unknown meaning. Saint Tatiana of Rome made it a favorite in Russia and Eastern Europe.
An American spelling of Dominic shaped by Italian Domenico, from Latin Dominicus, of the Lord. It was once given to boys born on Sunday, the Lord's day.
A respelling of Jason, from Greek Iason, linked to iasthai, to heal. In Greek myth Jason led the Argonauts in search of the Golden Fleece.
An early 1900s spelling of Grace, from Latin gratia, favor or thanks. Grace was one of the virtue names taken up by the Puritans.
A respelling of Addison, an English surname meaning son of Addie, a medieval pet form of Adam.
The Spanish, Italian and Polish form of Latin Delphina, woman of Delphi, the Greek city of the oracle. The place name is related to delphis, dolphin, and delphys, womb.
A spelling of Kiana, which is both the Hawaiian form of Diana and a modern American name of the 1980s and 90s.
An African American coinage, a variant of Jawan, close in sound to Juan and Dajuan. Basketball star Juwan Howard of Michigan's Fab Five carried it to its 1990s peak.
namesakes: Juwan Howard (NBA All-Star and member of Michigan's Fab Five)

e.etymology: A spelling of Paris and an English surname. The French capital is named for the Parisii, a Celtic tribe; Paris is also the Trojan prince of Greek myth who carried off Helen.

assoc.t: Parris Island, the Marine Corps boot camp in South Carolina

e.etymology: A spelling of Marnie, which probably began as a pet form of Marina or Marian. Alfred Hitchcock's 1964 film Marnie spread the name.
namesakes: Marni Nixon (singing voice in West Side Story and My Fair Lady)

e.etymology: A spelling of Kelsey, an English surname traced to the Old English personal name Ceolsige, from ceol, ship, and sige, victory.
The Spanish form of Blaise, from the Latin name Blasius, usually linked to blaesus, lisping or stammering. Saint Blaise, a fourth-century bishop, is the patron invoked for throat ailments.
An English surname built with ford, a river crossing. It is usually read as king's ford, since rex is Latin for king, and Rex is its short form.
A Kh spelling of Christopher, from Greek Christophoros, bearer of Christ. Legend tells of Saint Christopher carrying the Christ child across a river.
Latin oliva, olive or olive tree, used as a name in Italy and Spain and borne by several early saints. In American records it often appears as a variant of Olivia.
A French-styled spelling of Malik, Arabic for king or sovereign, taken up by African American families in the 1990s. Al-Malik, the King, is one of the names of God in Islam.
A spelling of Anna with the final h of Hannah. Both go back to Hebrew Channah, grace or favor.
A phonetic spelling of Xenia, from Greek xenia, hospitality, the welcome owed to a guest or stranger. Saint Xenia is honored in the Orthodox churches.
A shortened form of Adriana, the feminine of Adrian, from Latin Hadrianus, a man from Hadria, a town in northern Italy.
